q: How has God spoken in the past?
a: God has spoken in the past through the prophets at many times and in many ways.

q: How has God spoken in these recent days?
a: God has spoken in these recent days through a Son.

q: Through whom were the ages made?
a: The ages were made through the Son of God.

q: How are all things sustained?
a: All things are sustained by the word of the Son of God’s power.

q: How does the Son display the glory and essence of God?
a: The Son is the radiance of God’s glory and the representation of God’s essence.

q: How does the Son of God compare to the angels?
a: The Son of God is far superior to the angels.

q: What did God command the angels to do when the Son was brought into the world?
a: God commanded the angels to worship the Son when the Son was brought into the world.

q: How long will the Son rule as a king?
a: The Son will rule as a king for ever and ever.

q: What does the Son love and what does the Son hate?
a: The Son loves righteousness and the Son hates lawlessness.

q: What will happen to the earth and heavens over time?
a: The earth and heavens will wear out like a garment and perish.

q: Where did God tell the Son to sit, and until what happened?
a: God told the Son to sit at his right hand until God made the Son’s enemies a stool for the Son’s feet.

q: For whom do the angels care?
a: The angels care for those who are going to inherit salvation.

q: Why must believers pay attention to what they have heard?
a: Believers must pay attention to what they have heard so that they do not drift away from it.

q: What would every transgression and disobedience receive?
a: Every transgression and disobedience would receive just punishment.

q: How did God testify to the message of salvation announced by the Lord?
a: God testified to the message by signs, wonders, powerful deeds, and by the gifts of the Holy Spirit.

q: Who will not rule the world to come?
a: Angels will not rule the world to come.

q: Who will rule the world to come?
a: Man will rule the world to come.

q: Why was Jesus crowned with glory and honor?
a: Jesus was crowned with glory and honor because of his suffering and death.

q: For whom did Jesus taste death?
a: Jesus tasted death for every man.

q: Whom does God plan to bring to glory?
a: God plans to bring many sons to glory.

q: Who are the two who come from the one source, God?
a: Both the one who sanctifies and those who are sanctified come from the one source, God.

q: Who was made ineffective through Jesus’ death?
a: The devil was made ineffective through Jesus’ death.

q: From what slavery are people freed through the death of Jesus?
a: Through the death of Jesus, people are freed from the fear of death.

q: Why was it necessary for Jesus to be like his brothers in all ways?
a: It was necessary so that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest over God’s things, and so he might obtain forgiveness for the people’s sins.

q: Why is Jesus able to help those who are tempted?
a: Jesus is able to help those who are tempted because he was tempted also.

q: What two roles does the author of the book of Hebrews say Jesus fills?
a: The author says Jesus is an apostle and a high priest.

q: Why has Jesus been considered worthy of greater glory than Moses?
a: Jesus has been considered worthy of greater glory because, while Moses was faithful in all God’s house, Jesus is the one who built the house.

q: What was Moses’ role in God’s house?
a: Moses was a servant in God’s house.

q: About what did Moses give testimony?
a: Moses gave testimony about the things that were to be spoken of in the future.

q: What is Jesus’ role in God’s house?
a: Jesus’ role is as a Son in charge of God’s house.

q: Who is God’s house?
a: The believers are God’s house if they hold fast to their confidence.

q: What did the Israelites in the wilderness do when they heard God’s voice?
a: The Israelites hardened their hearts.

q: What did God swear concerning the Israelites who went astray in their hearts?
a: God swore that they would not enter his rest.

q: Of what are the brothers warned to be careful?
a: The brothers are warned to be careful not to turn away from the living God by unbelief.

q: What are the brothers to do in order to avoid being hardened by the deceitfulness of sin?
a: The brothers are to encourage one another daily.

q: As partners of Christ, what must believers do?
a: As partners of Christ, believers must firmly hold their confidence in him from the beginning to the end.

q: With whom was God angry for 40 years?
a: God was angry with those who sinned in the wilderness.

q: What happened to those with whom God was angry?
a: Their dead bodies lay in the wilderness.

q: Why were the disobedient Israelites not able to enter God’s rest?
a: They were not able to enter God’s rest, because of unbelief.

q: What good news had the believers and the Israelites both heard?
a: The believers and the Israelites had both heard the good news about God’s rest.

q: Why did the good news not benefit the Israelites?
a: The good news did not benefit the Israelites because they did not join in faith with those who believed it.

q: When did God finish his created works and then rest?
a: God finished his created works at the beginning of the world and then rested on the seventh day.

q: Who are the ones who enter God’s rest?
a: Those who have believed enter God’s rest.

q: What did God say about the Israelites and his rest?
a: God said that the Israelites would not enter his rest.

q: What day has God now set for people to enter his rest?
a: God has set “Today” as the day for people to enter his rest.

q: What must a person do in order to enter God’s rest?
a: A person must listen to God’s voice and not harden his heart.

q: What is still reserved for God’s people?
a: A Sabbath rest is still reserved for God’s people.

q: A person who enters God’s rest also rests from what?
a: A person who enters God’s rest also rests from his works.

q: Why should believers be eager to enter God’s rest?
a: Believers should be eager to enter God’s rest so that they do not fall into disobedience as the Israelites did.

q: What is the word of God sharper than?
a: The word of God is sharper than any two-edged sword.

q: What is the Word of God able to divide?
a: The Word of God is able to divide soul from spirit and joints from marrow.

q: What is the Word of God able to discern?
a: The Word of God is able to discern the thoughts and intentions of the heart.

q: Who or what is hidden from God’s sight?
a: No created thing is hidden from God’s sight.

q: Who serves as the great high priest for believers?
a: Jesus, the Son of God, serves as the great high priest for believers.

q: Why does Jesus feel sympathy for the weaknesses of believers?
a: Jesus feels sympathy for the weaknesses of believers because he was in all ways tempted.

q: How many times did Jesus sin?
a: Jesus never sinned. Jesus was without sin.

q: In time of need, what are believers to do to receive mercy and find grace?
a: In time of need, believers are to approach with confidence to the throne of grace.

q: What does every high priest do on behalf of the people?
a: For the people, every high priest offers gifts and sacrifices for sins.

q: In addition to the people, for whom does the high priest also present sacrifices?
a: The high priest also presents sacrifices for his own sins.

q: How does a man receive the honor of being a high priest of God?
a: A man must be called by God to be a high priest of God.

q: Who declared Christ to be a high priest?
a: God declared Christ to be a high priest.

q: For how long is Christ God’s high priest?
a: Christ is God’s high priest forever.

q: Of what order is Christ as a high priest?
a: Christ is a high priest of the order of Melchizedek.

q: Why was Christ heard by God when he prayed?
a: Christ was heard by God because of his godly life.

q: How did Christ learn obedience?
a: Christ learned obedience from the things he suffered.

q: For whom did Christ become the cause of eternal salvation?
a: For everyone who obeys him, Christ became the cause of their eternal salvation.

q: What was the spiritual condition of the original readers of this letter?
a: The original readers were dull of hearing.

q: How does the author of the letter say that believers grow from spiritual babies into full-grown adults?
a: Believers grow spiritually by practicing distinguishing right from wrong, discerning both good and evil.

q: What teachings does the author list as the foundation of the message of Christ?
a: The foundational teachings are repentance from dead works, faith in God, baptisms, laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.

q: On to what does the author of Hebrews want the believers to go forward?
a: The author of Hebrews wants the believers to go forward to maturity.

q: What is impossible for those who gained so much in Christ but then fell away, to do?
a: It is impossible for those who gained so much in Christ, but then fell away, to be restored again to repentance.

q: What had these enlightened people gained?
a: These enlightened people had tasted the heavenly gift, became sharers of the Holy Spirit, and tasted God’s Word and the powers of the age to come.

q: Why are these people not able to be restored to repentance?
a: They are not able to be restored because they have crucified for themselves the very Son of God and exposed him to public shame.

q: In the author’s analogy, what happens to land that receives rain but bears thorns and thistles?
a: Land that receives rain but bears thorns and thistles has its end in burning.

q: What is the author’s expectation concerning the believers to whom he is writing?
a: The author expects better things concerning these believers, things that are about salvation.

q: What will God not forget about these believers?
a: God will not forget their work, love of God, and service to the saints.

q: What should the believers imitate about those who inherit the promises of God?
a: The believers should imitate the faith and patience of those who inherit the promises of God.

q: What did Abraham have to do in order to obtain what God promised him?
a: Abraham had to wait patiently to obtain what God promised him.

q: Why did God guarantee his promise with an oath?
a: God guaranteed his promise with an oath to show more clearly the unchangeable quality of his purpose.

q: What is it impossible for God to do?
a: It is impossible for God to lie.

q: Where did Jesus enter as the forerunner for the believers?
a: Jesus entered into the inner place behind the curtain as the forerunner for the believers.

q: What does the believer’s hope in God do for his soul?
a: The believer’s hope in God is a secure and reliable anchor for his soul.

q: What two titles did Melchizedek have?
a: Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High.

q: What did Abraham give Melchizedek?
a: Abraham gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything he had captured.

q: What does the name Melchizedek mean?
a: The name Melchizedek means “king of righteousness” and “king of peace.”

q: Who were the ancestors of Melchizedek, and when did he die?
a: Melchizedek was without ancestors and has no end of life.

q: From whom are the priests descended who are priests according to the Law and who collect tithes from the people?
a: The priests of the Law are descended from Levi, and before him, from Abraham.

q: Who was the greater person, Abraham or Melchizedek?
a: Melchizedek was the greater person because he blessed Abraham.

q: In what way did Levi himself also pay tithes to Melchizedek?
a: Levi also paid tithes to Melchizedek, because Levi was of the seed of Abraham, and Abraham paid tithes to Melchizedek.

q: What must also be changed when the priesthood changes?
a: The law must be changed when the priesthood changes.

q: From which tribe did Jesus descend, and had this tribe served before at the altar as priests?
a: Jesus descended from the tribe of Judah, which had never before served at the altar as priests.

q: On what basis did Jesus become a priest after the order of Melchizedek?
a: Jesus became a priest after the order of Melchizedek based on the power of an indestructible life.

q: What has been set aside because it is weak and useless?
a: The former commandment, the Law, has been set aside because it is weak and useless.

q: What oath did God swear concerning Jesus?
a: God swore that Jesus would be a priest forever.

q: Of what is Jesus the guarantee?
a: Jesus is the guarantee of a better covenant.

q: Why is Jesus able to completely save those who draw near to God through him?
a: Jesus is able to completely save those who draw near to God through him because he always lives to intercede for them.

q: What four attributes does Jesus have that make him the right priest for believers?
a: Jesus is holy, innocent, pure, and separated from sinners.

q: What offering did Jesus need to make for his own sins?
a: Jesus did not need to make any offering for his own sins, because he is sinless.

q: What offering did Jesus make for the sins of the people?
a: Jesus offered up himself once for the sins of the people.

q: How is Jesus different from the priests who were appointed through the Law?
a: The priests who were appointed through the Law were weak, but Jesus has been made perfect forever.

q: Where is the believers’ high priest sitting?
a: The believers’ high priest is sitting at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens.

q: Where is the true tabernacle?
a: The true tabernacle is in the heavens.

q: What is necessary for every priest to have?
a: Every priest must have something to offer.

q: Where were the priests who offered gifts according to the Law?
a: The priests who offered gifts according to the Law were on the earth.

q: What did the priests on earth serve?
a: The priests on earth served an example and a shadow of the heavenly things.

q: According to what pattern was the earthly tabernacle built?
a: The earthly tabernacle was built according to the pattern God showed Moses on the mountain.

q: Why does Christ have a superior priestly ministry?
a: Christ has a superior priestly ministry because he is the mediator of a better covenant, established on better promises.

q: What did God promise when he found fault with the people under the first covenant?
a: God promised to make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.

q: What did God say he would do in the new covenant?
a: God said he would put his laws into the people’s minds, and write them on their hearts.

q: In the new covenant, who will know the Lord?
a: In the new covenant, all will know the Lord, from the least to the greatest.

q: What did God say he would do with the people’s sins in the new covenant?
a: God said he would remember the people’s sins no more.

q: In announcing a new covenant, what did God make the first covenant?
a: In announcing a new covenant, God made the first covenant obsolete, growing old and disappearing.

q: What was the place of worship for the first covenant?
a: The place of worship for the first covenant was the earthly holy place which was called the “tabernacle.”

q: What was located in the holy place of the earthly tabernacle?
a: In the holy place of the earthly tabernacle were the lampstand, the table, and the bread of the presence.

q: What was located in the most holy place of the earthly tabernacle?
a: In the most holy place of the earthly tabernacle were the altar for incense and the ark of the covenant.

q: How often did the high priest enter the Holy of Holies, and what did he do before he entered?
a: The high priest entered the Holy of Holies once each year, after making a blood sacrifice for himself and the people.

q: What served as an illustration in the present time for the readers of this letter?
a: The earthly tabernacle and the gifts and sacrifices being offered there served as an illustration in the present time.

q: What were the offerings of the earthly tabernacle not able to do?
a: The offerings of the earthly tabernacle were not able to perfect the worshiper’s conscience.

q: Until when were the regulations of the earthly tabernacle provided?
a: The regulations of the earthly tabernacle were provided until the new order would be put in place.

q: What is different about the sacred tent in which Christ serves?
a: The sacred tent in which Christ serves is more perfect, is not made by human hands, and does not belong to this created world.

q: What offering did Christ make, by which he entered the Holy of Holies?
a: Christ made an offering of his own blood by which he entered the Holy of Holies.

q: What did Christ’s offering accomplish?
a: Christ’s offering secured everlasting redemption for everyone.

q: What does Christ’s blood do for the believer?
a: Christ’s blood cleanses the believer’s conscience from dead deeds to serve the living God.

q: Of what is Christ the mediator?
a: Christ is the mediator of a new covenant.

q: What is required in order for a will to be in force?
a: A death is required in order for a will to be in force.

q: What death was required for the first covenant?
a: The death of calves and goats was required for the first covenant.

q: What cannot happen without the shedding of blood?
a: Without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness of sins.

q: Where does Christ now appear on our behalf?
a: Christ now appears in heaven itself, in the presence of God, on our behalf.

q: How many times must Christ offer himself to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself?
a: Christ offers himself one time, at the end of the ages, to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.

q: For every person, what happens after their death?
a: After every person dies, they face the judgment.

q: For what purpose will Christ appear a second time?
a: Christ will appear a second time for the salvation of those who wait eagerly for him.

q: What is the law as compared to the realities in Christ?
a: The law is only a shadow of the realities in Christ.

q: Of what do the repeated sacrifices made through the law remind the worshipers?
a: The repeated sacrifices made through the law remind the worshipers of sins committed year after year.

q: What is it impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to do?
a: It is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.

q: What did God prepare for Christ when Christ came into the world?
a: God prepared a body for Christ.

q: What practice did God set aside when Christ came into the world?
a: God set aside the first practice of the sacrifices offered according to the law.

q: What practice did God establish when Christ came into the world?
a: God established the second practice of the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

q: For what is Christ waiting as he sits at the right side of God?
a: Christ is waiting until his enemies are humbled and made a stool for his feet.

q: By his one offering, what has Christ done for those sanctified?
a: Christ has perfected forever those who are sanctified by his one offering.

q: What is no longer required where there is forgiveness of sins?
a: Additional sacrifices are no longer required where there is forgiveness of sins.

q: Into what place can believers now enter by Jesus’ blood?
a: Believers can now enter the most holy place by Jesus’ blood.

q: What has been sprinkled and what has been washed in the believer?
a: The believer’s heart has been sprinkled clean from an evil conscience, and his body has been washed with pure water.

q: To what must believers hold tightly?
a: Believers must hold tightly to the confession of their hope.

q: What must believers do as they see the day drawing near?
a: Believers must encourage one another more and more as they see the day drawing near.

q: What is the expectation of those who deliberately go on sinning after receiving the knowledge of the truth?
a: The expectation of those who deliberately go on sinning after receiving the knowledge of the truth is judgment and a fiery zeal that consumes God’s enemies.

q: What does the person deserve who treats the blood of Christ, by which he was sanctified, as something unholy?
a: The person who treats the blood of Christ by which he was sanctified as something unholy deserves punishment without mercy beyond the punishment given under the law of Moses.

q: To whom does vengeance belong?
a: Vengeance belongs to the Lord.

q: How had the believers who received this letter reacted to the seizure of their possessions?
a: The believers had accepted with joy the seizure of their possessions, knowing they had a better and everlasting possession.

q: What must the believer need not throw away so he may receive what God has promised?
a: The believer needs to retain his confidence so he may receive what God has promised.

q: How will the righteous live?
a: The righteous will live by faith.

q: What does God think of those who shrink back?
a: God is not pleased with those who shrink back.

q: What is the author’s expectation for those who received this letter?
a: The author’s expectation is that those who received this letter will have faith for keeping their souls.

q: What attitude does a person of faith have toward God’s promises that are yet to be fulfilled?
a: A person of faith confidently expects and has certainty toward God’s promises that are yet to be fulfilled.

q: From what were the visible things of the universe created?
a: The visible things of the universe were not made out of things that were visible.

q: Why did God praise Abel for being righteous?
a: God praised Abel because Abel by faith offered God a more appropriate sacrifice than Cain did.

q: What must one who comes to God believe about God?
a: One who comes to God must believe that God exists and that he rewards those who seek him.

q: How did Noah demonstrate his faith?
a: Noah demonstrated his faith by building an ark to save his family according to God’s warning.

q: What promise did Abraham and Sarah receive by faith?
a: Abraham and Sarah received by faith the power to conceive even when they were too old.

q: What did the ancestors of faith see from far off?
a: The ancestors of faith saw and welcomed God’s promises from far off.

q: What did the ancestors of faith consider themselves on the earth?
a: The ancestors of faith considered themselves strangers and aliens on the earth.

q: What has God prepared for those of faith?
a: God has prepared a heavenly city for those of faith.

q: What did Abraham believe God would be able to do even as he offered up Isaac his only son?
a: Abraham believed God would be able to raise up Isaac from the dead.

q: What did Joseph prophesy by faith when his end was near?
a: Joseph prophesied of the departure of the children of Israel from Egypt when his end was near.

q: What did Moses choose to do by faith when he had grown up?
a: Moses chose by faith to share mistreatment with God’s people, considering the disgrace of following Christ as greater riches.

q: What did Moses observe by faith in order to save the Israelites’ firstborn sons?
a: Moses observed the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood by faith in order to save the Israelites’ firstborn sons.

q: What did Rahab do by faith which prevented her from perishing?
a: Rahab by faith received the spies in safety, which prevented her from perishing.

q: What did some of the ancestors of faith accomplish in war?
a: Some of the ancestors of faith conquered kingdoms, escaped the sword, became mighty in war, and caused foreign armies to flee.

q: What did some of the ancestors of faith suffer?
a: Some of the ancestors of faith suffered torture, mocking, whippings, chains, imprisonments, stoning, sawing in two, death, and destitution.

q: Despite the faith of these ancestors, what did they not receive in their earthly lives?
a: Despite the faith of these ancestors, they did not receive in their earthly lives what God had promised them.

q: With whom will the ancestors of faith receive the promises of God and be perfected?
a: The ancestors of faith will receive the promises of God and be perfected with the new covenant believers in Christ.

q: Why should the believer throw off the sin that easily entangles him?
a: The believer should throw off the sin that easily entangles him in order to run with endurance the race placed before him.

q: Why did Jesus endure the cross and despise its shame?
a: Jesus endured the cross and despised its shame for the joy that was set before him.

q: How can a believer avoid becoming weary or fainthearted?
a: By considering Jesus, who endured hateful speech from sinners, a believer can avoid becoming weary or fainthearted.

q: What does the Lord do to those whom he loves and receives?
a: The Lord disciplines those whom he loves and receives.

q: What is a person who is without the Lord’s discipline?
a: A person without the Lord’s discipline is an illegitimate child and not God’s child.

q: Why does God discipline his children?
a: God disciplines his children for their good, so they can share in his holiness.

q: What does discipline produce?
a: Discipline produces peaceful fruit of righteousness.

q: What should believers pursue with all people?
a: Believers should pursue peace with all people.

q: What must not grow up and cause trouble and pollute many?
a: A root of bitterness must not grow up and cause trouble and pollute many.

q: What happened to Esau when he desired to inherit the blessing with tears after selling his own birthright?
a: Esau was rejected when he desired to inherit the blessing with tears after selling his own birthright.

q: For what did the Israelites beg at the mountain where God spoke?
a: The Israelites begged that not another word be spoken to them.

q: To where do believers in Christ come instead of the mountain where the Israelites heard the voice of God?
a: Believers in Christ come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God.

q: To whom do believers in Christ come?
a: Believer in Christ come to God, the Judge of all, to the spirits of the righteous, and to Jesus.

q: To what assembly do believers in Christ come?
a: Believers in Christ come to the assembly of all the firstborn registered in heaven.

q: What will happen to those who turn away from the one who warns them from heaven?
a: Those who turn away will not escape from God.

q: What has God promised to shake?
a: God has promised to shake the earth and the heaven.

q: What will the believers receive instead of the things that can be shaken?
a: The believers will receive a kingdom that cannot be shaken.

q: How should believers serve God?
a: Believers should serve God with reverence and awe.

q: Why should believers worship God in this way?
a: Believers should worship God in this way because he is a consuming fire.

q: What have some done by welcoming strangers?
a: Some have welcomed angels without knowing it.

q: How should believers remember those in prison?
a: Believers should remember them as if they were in prison also, and as if their bodies were being mistreated also.

q: What must be respected by all?
a: Marriage must be respected by all.

q: What does God do with the sexually immoral and adulterers?
a: God judges the sexually immoral and adulterers.

q: How can a believer be free from the love of money?
a: A believer can be free from the love of money because God has said he will never leave nor forsake him.

q: Who’s faith should believers imitate?
a: Believers should imitate the faith of those who have led them and who have spoken God’s Word to them.

q: About what kind of strange teachings does the author warn the believers?
a: The author warns the believers about strange teachings involving rules about food.

q: Where were the bodies of the animals used for sacrifice in the holy place burned?
a: The bodies of the animals were burned outside the camp.

q: Where did Jesus suffer?
a: Jesus suffered outside the city gate.

q: Where must believers go, and why?
a: Believers must go to Jesus outside the camp, bearing his disgrace.

q: What permanent city do believers have here on earth?
a: Believers have no permanent city here on earth. They seek the one coming.

q: What city do believers seek instead?
a: Believers seek the city that is to come.

q: What sacrifice should believers constantly offer up to God?
a: Believers should constantly offer up a sacrifice of praise to God.

q: What attitude should believers have toward their leaders?
a: Believers should obey and submit to their leaders.

q: What does God work in the believer?
a: God works in the believer that which is well pleasing in God’s sight.

q: With whom will the author come when he visits the believers?
a: The author will come with Timothy when he visits the believers.
